slot_note: wave 3, seed DQ14 (which domain estimates fail the calibration margin check and are reissued); the seed's survey pairing is banned against task240, so the world moved to a sensor-calibration release: which floats' salinity records the delayed-mode release adjusts
niche: a national ocean institute's delayed-mode quality control of its regional profiling-float array: which floats' 2027 salinity records the delayed-mode release adjusts, each float's conductivity-sensor offset read against ship reference casts in the deep water below the Mediterranean outflow
answer: Adjust the 2027 salinity of six of the 24 floats in the delayed-mode release: 1990001, 1990004, 1990005 and 1990008, which read fresh (offsets -0.022, -0.020, -0.027, -0.030), and 1990007 and 1990012, which read salty (+0.021, +0.020). The other 18 floats' 2027 salinity goes out as measured.
stakeholder_role: the array's delayed-mode quality-control operator at the institute's ocean data centre

spine.entity: one pressure level of one float profile file
spine.grain: float x cycle x file version x level

world.geography: Portugal, the Iberian Basin of the eastern North Atlantic (a fictional national ocean institute and its float array; real ocean geography)
world.org_type: national ocean research institute running a regional profiling-float array and its data centre

driver: The decisive quantity is a sensor's own error read against an external reference whose value at a fixed position in the medium moves with a displacement of the medium that the reference years did not share and with a slow drift of the medium's properties across the area, so the error has to be read on a coordinate the displacement carries with it and against reference medium from the sensor's own place; read at fixed position against the area's average, the medium's shift and its gradient are taken for sensor error, and both false flags and misses follow.
driver_concrete: A float's conductivity offset is the difference between the salinity it reported and the true salinity of the water it sampled; below the Mediterranean outflow the deep layer heaves with eddies and sat deeper in 2027 than in the reference years, while the salinity of water at a given temperature falls westward as the outflow thins, so comparing at fixed pressure, or on temperature levels against the whole basin's reference, takes heave and position for sensor error; only the salinity on potential temperature levels against reference water at the profile's own position isolates the sensor.
stump: A competent analyst differences each float's good 2027 salinity values between 1,400 and 1,900 dbar against the reference casts' mean salinity at the same pressure and files 14 of the 24 floats adjusted, the six whose sensors are off and eight whose sensors read true; the step that lands it there is comparing at fixed pressure, when the deep layer sat deeper in 2027 than in the reference years and heaved with eddies and the salinity of water at a given temperature falls westward, so only the offset on potential-temperature levels against reference water at each profile's own position gives the six.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every flag and file correctly, keeps the good 2027 ascending profiles and differences each float's salinity against the reference casts' salinity at the same pressures over the 1,400 to 1,900 dbar layer adjusts 14 floats (eight of them clean); one who compares on potential-temperature levels against the basin's pooled reference adjusts 10 to 14, and one who measures drift from each float's first profiles finds only the four drifting floats; only potential-temperature levels against reference water at each profile's position give the six.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each float's conductivity-sensor offset estimated the way delayed-mode quality control of profiling floats estimates it, against ship CTD reference data on potential-temperature levels where the deep water masses' temperature-salinity relation is conserved, mapped to the float's position; with hospital thermometers or meter readings in place of ocean profiles there is no water column that heaves, no water mass whose temperature fixes its salinity and no basin-scale property gradient, so the task stops making sense.

differentiation.task148: task148 (v2) estimates queue patience from censored waits for a demand forecast; task241 reads a float sensor's salinity error against reference water on the coordinate that heave carries, at the float's own position: no quantity, mechanism or file shared

notes: Seed DQ14: the decision (the reissue list of a release) and the quantity (each estimate against a calibration margin) kept; the seed's world (raking margins in a survey release) and its pairing are banned against task240, so the release is an ocean data centre's delayed-mode salinity adjustment. The seed's pitfall (one raking pass) is not used. Built: the golden adjusts six floats (four drifting fresh, two salty from deployment); the default path (fixed pressure against the casts' mean) adjusts 14 (13 to 17 across implementations), the pooled temperature-level reference 10 to 14, drift from the first profiles 4; asks: reference casts reaching 2,000 dbar by year (RHD copies of the institute's casts) and on-time complete deliveries by month (model K's profile time at the start of the ascent).
layer1: profiles at two grains (the profile index with each profile's time as days since 1950 in UTC and its position, the level file with pressure in dbar), joined on the decoded file's id
real-time quality flags on every value (1 good to 4 bad), salinity spikes flagged

descending profiles beside the ascending ones from four floats, and a partner institute's float decoded beside the array

reference casts from the institute's archive (the 2015 and 2016 cruises in IPTS-68) and an international extract (depth in metres, positions to 0.01 degree, decimal-hour times, the institute's own casts again under the database's ids)
